The *Mohapariññā Sutta* (Iti 11; PTS It 6) is a short discourse preserved in the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The text teaches that when the mind is cleansed of passion for delusion and abandons it, one is capable of putting an end to suffering [SuttaCentral].
According to SuttaCentral, a curated full parallel exists in the Chinese translation of the *Itivuttaka* at T 765.39 (愚癡) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus highlights extensive structural sharing with closely related discourses in the *Itivuttaka* on abandoning defilements, most notably the *Makkhapariññā Sutta* (Iti 13), *Kodhapariññā Sutta* (Iti 12), *Lobhapariññā Sutta* (Iti 9), and *Dosapariññā Sutta* (Iti 10) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects substantial reuse across 12 passages in the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), along with an automatic cross-language alignment to a section of the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
